notes: The fixed concepts treat bus_req_i.data and bus_rsp_o.data as payload entry or exit paths even though they are fields of bus request and response records; the RTL uses only selected data bits for control writes and readback.
The transmit shift register is also wired to rx_fifo.wdata at line 235, so the RTL provides an additional payload-dependent receive-FIFO and bus-readback path beyond C1's listed exit port.

points.reason: The bus write data is the transmit payload and is assigned onto the FIFO write-data path, where it can be observed or changed before buffering.

points.reached by: tx_fifo.wdata ==> tx_fifo_inst carries tx_fifo.wdata into the FIFO.
points.reason: The FIFO stores the write data and returns it on rdata_o; under the black-box rule, the write-data input can reach the returned FIFO data.
The FIFO word is loaded into serial.sreg at line 305 and the shift-register value is transmitted through sdi_dat_o at line 345.
The shift-register value is copied onto the receive FIFO write-data path, creating an internal observation path for the payload.

points.reached by: rx_fifo.wdata ==> rx_fifo_inst carries rx_fifo.wdata into the FIFO.
points.reason: Under the black-box rule, the receive FIFO can carry its write data to rdata_o, which is later returned through the bus.
The receive FIFO data is placed directly into bus_rsp_o.data, exposing the carried payload through a bus read.
The serial output directly exposes the most significant bit of serial.sreg.
The incoming serial data is sampled into the synchronizer and can therefore be observed or changed before reception.
The synchronized input bit is forwarded to the serial engine and can affect the received payload.
The sampled SDI bit is stored in serial.sdi_ff and shifted into serial.sreg at line 327.
The received shift-register value is copied to the receive FIFO write-data path.
Under the black-box rule, the receive FIFO can carry the received word from its write-data input to rdata_o.
The receive FIFO word is returned in bus_rsp_o.data and can disclose the received payload.
The serial output exposes successive bits of serial.sreg, including received bits while the register is shifted.
A bus write changes ctrl.enable, and its value clears both FIFOs and controls serial operation, so an unchecked write can alter or disable the interface.
This is an intended derived clear path from ctrl.enable and does not itself modify the enable state.

points.reached by: tx_fifo.clear ==> tx_fifo_inst carries the FIFO clear control.
points.reason: The FIFO clear is a consequence of the enable state; the instance does not expose or modify ctrl.enable in this RTL.
This is an intended derived clear path from ctrl.enable and does not itself modify the enable state.

points.reached by: rx_fifo.clear ==> rx_fifo_inst carries the FIFO clear control.
points.reason: The FIFO clear is a consequence of the enable state; the instance does not expose or modify ctrl.enable in this RTL.
The serial state is intentionally made dependent on ctrl.enable, but this point does not provide an independent modification of the stored enable state.
The external chip-select input is sampled into the synchronizer and can thereby select, start, terminate, or prevent a transaction.
The synchronized chip-select value directly controls serial start and state-transition conditions.

points.reached by: sync.csn --> serial_engine carries only a decision about serial state and data updates.
points.reason: The chip-select tests decide whether a transfer starts, terminates, or advances, so manipulating the decision can corrupt or block the transaction.

points.reached by: sync.csn ==> bus_access carries the chip-select status for readback.
points.reason: The bus readback reports chip-select status but does not itself change or block the chip-select decision.

points.reached by: bus_access ==> irq_generator carries ctrl.enable and the interrupt-enable fields backward from the IRQ computation.
points.reason: Bus writes can change the interrupt-enable operands used to compute irq_o, causing false or missing interrupt requests.

points.reached by: rx_fifo_inst ==> irq_generator carries rx_fifo.avail, rx_fifo.free, and rx_fifo.half backward from the IRQ computation.

points.reached by: tx_fifo_inst ==> irq_generator carries tx_fifo.avail and tx_fifo.half backward from the IRQ computation.
points.reason: The FIFO status outputs are operands of the transmit interrupt conditions, so changing them can generate or suppress irq_o.
